comment: Each verdict compares the byte-pinned paper-source bundle with Lean's current semantic target and exact bounded declaration code. These prerequisites are not additional paper-claim rows.

AppliedModelingLib.IsJointlySmoothGradie.label: AppliedModelingLib.IsJointlySmoothGradient
AppliedModelingLib.IsJointlySmoothGradie.reason: The expanded definition is exactly the two A1 Lipschitz inequalities for the supplied gradient: uniform smoothness in the parameter coordinate and, through IsDataGradientLipschitz, in the data coordinate. Its graph-bound uses separately require HasGradientAt to identify this field with the loss gradient, and the definition's global parameter/data quantifiers are the stronger scope expressly disclosed in the corrected Theorem 3.10 target.

AppliedModelingLib.IsMeasureDataLossLips.label: AppliedModelingLib.IsMeasureDataLossLipschitz
AppliedModelingLib.IsMeasureDataLossLips.reason: The expanded definition requires one NNReal constant to make the loss Lipschitz in the data coordinate for every ambient parameter. This is exactly the globally scoped RERM Wasserstein-to-loss bridge expressly included in the corrected Theorem 3.10(a) premise bundle and used with the same model and constant.

AppliedModelingLib.IsMeasurePointwiseGra.label: AppliedModelingLib.IsMeasurePointwiseGradientStronglyConvex
AppliedModelingLib.IsMeasurePointwiseGra.reason: The expanded definition states the A2 lower bound with modulus / 2 times squared parameter distance for every datum, center, and candidate, using the supplied gradient at the center. The graph-bound carriers separately identify that gradient with HasGradientAt; the all-ambient quantifier scope is exactly the stronger scope disclosed by the corrected target.

AppliedModelingLib.IsMeasureWassersteinS.label: AppliedModelingLib.IsMeasureWassersteinSensitive
AppliedModelingLib.IsMeasureWassersteinS.reason: For every pair of ambient parameters, the expanded definition supplies a finite expected-distance coupling and bounds the resulting real W1 infimum by sensitivity times parameter distance. This is the finite-first-moment Wasserstein-1 reading and global scope expressly disclosed in the corrected Theorem 3.10 premises and used unchanged by the carriers.

AppliedModelingLib.MeasurePerformativeMo.label: AppliedModelingLib.MeasurePerformativeModel
AppliedModelingLib.MeasurePerformativeMo.reason: The expanded structure consists of a probability data law for every deployed parameter, a loss for every datum and evaluated parameter, and integrability of that loss under every deployed/evaluated pair. Those are exactly the globally defined model and expected-loss integrability conditions disclosed in the corrected Theorem 3.10 target and assumed by every displayed material use.

AppliedModelingLib.MeasurePerformativeMo.label: AppliedModelingLib.MeasurePerformativeModelOn
AppliedModelingLib.MeasurePerformativeMo.reason: Compared domain_relative_performative_model at cited publication:151-172,188-194,219-228 with the three record-field displays and every listed risk/predicate/use display. dataLaw is a fixed probability-law map on Theta, and loss has a datum and a feasible parameter as its arguments. The independently quantified distributionParameter and evaluatedParameter in loss_integrable cover exactly the two parameters of the source DPR expectation, with PR as its diagonal. These fields give the source risks as real expectations without requiring a distribution or loss value outside Theta. The displayed paper use supplies closedness and convexity of the domain, a positive A2 modulus, the uniform data-Lipschitz and nonnegative sensitivity hypotheses, and the optimal/stable domain members. Its A2 prerequisite binds the loss derivative within this same domain; the explicit zero extension is read only within the domain and therefore adds no off-domain regularity condition.
AppliedModelingLib.MeasurePerformativeMo.source_location: cited publication:151-172; cited publication:188-194; cited publication:219-228

AppliedModelingLib.MeasurePerformativeMo.label: AppliedModelingLib.MeasurePerformativeModelOn.IsDataLossLipschitz
AppliedModelingLib.MeasurePerformativeMo.reason: Compared theorem_4_3_data_lipschitz_premise at cited publication:468-480 with the expanded predicate, model fields, and theorem-use display. For every parameter in Theta, the same constant bounds the Lipschitz modulus of datum -> loss datum parameter. Thus the target is the uniform data-coordinate inequality |loss(z,theta)-loss(z-prime,theta)| <= Lz dist(z,z-prime), as required by the source premise. The NNReal parameter permits Lz=0 and supplies its nonnegativity; no parameter-coordinate Lipschitz condition is introduced. The use retains this same constant and the domain membership of all parameters. Model integrability provides the real expectations required by the displayed risk comparisons.
AppliedModelingLib.MeasurePerformativeMo.source_location: cited publication:468-480 (PMLR PDF p. 7, Theorem 4.3 premise)

AppliedModelingLib.MeasurePerformativeMo.label: AppliedModelingLib.MeasurePerformativeModelOn.IsPerformativelyOptimal
AppliedModelingLib.MeasurePerformativeMo.reason: Compared definition_2_1_performative_optimality_and_risk at cited publication:161-172 with the expanded predicate, both risk definitions, the model fields, and the listed theorem use. Expanding the two risk definitions gives E under D(optimal) of loss(Z,optimal) <= E under D(candidate) of loss(Z,candidate) for every candidate in Theta. Both the law and evaluation argument vary together on the candidate side, exactly the source argmin of PR. The supplied optimal member satisfies all comparisons; neither this predicate nor its paper use asserts uniqueness or constructs an optimum. The model covers the integrability of every diagonal expectation, and all minimization arguments stay inside the source domain.

AppliedModelingLib.MeasurePerformativeMo.label: AppliedModelingLib.MeasurePerformativeModelOn.IsPerformativelyStable
AppliedModelingLib.MeasurePerformativeMo.reason: Compared definition_2_3_performative_stability_and_decoupled_risk at cited publication:219-228 with the expanded predicate and all listed model, decoupled-risk, and theorem-use displays. The resulting inequality is E under D(stable) of loss(Z,stable) <= E under D(stable) of loss(Z,candidate) for every candidate in Theta. The induced distribution is fixed on both sides, and only the evaluated classifier changes, exactly the source argmin_theta DPR(thetaPS,theta). The supplied stable domain member need not be unique, and no existence assertion is substituted for the predicate. Universal cross-law integrability in the model covers these fixed-law real expectations.

AppliedModelingLib.MeasurePerformativeMo.label: AppliedModelingLib.MeasurePerformativeModelOn.IsPointwiseGradientStronglyConvex
AppliedModelingLib.MeasurePerformativeMo.reason: Compared the A2 formula in assumptions_a1_a2_joint_smoothness_and_strong_convexity at cited publication:270-282 with the full expanded conjunctive predicate, its model prerequisite, and the theorem-4.3 use. For every datum and feasible center, HasFDerivWithinAt identifies the derivative of the loss on Theta with the linear functional v -> inner(gradient datum center,v). The subsequent inequality uses exactly this same vector, every feasible candidate, the displacement candidate-center, and modulus/2 times its squared norm. This gives the actual first-order quadratic lower model in source A2 rather than an unrestricted supporting-vector condition. The zero extension agrees with the loss at every point used by the within-domain derivative, so it imposes no differentiability outside Theta or discontinuity condition across its boundary. On lower-dimensional domains, any undetermined normal component has zero pairing with feasible displacements and does not change A2. The paper use requires this whole predicate and a strictly positive modulus on its closed convex domain; A1 smoothness is not inadvertently added. In particular, theta^2+|theta| on [-1,1] cannot satisfy the derivative conjunct at its interior point 0.
AppliedModelingLib.MeasurePerformativeMo.source_location: cited publication:270-282 (PMLR PDF p. 4, A1 and A2)

AppliedModelingLib.MeasurePerformativeMo.label: AppliedModelingLib.MeasurePerformativeModelOn.IsWassersteinSensitive
AppliedModelingLib.MeasurePerformativeMo.reason: Compared definition_3_1_epsilon_sensitivity at cited publication:242-249 with the expanded predicate and every listed coupling/model/use display. The joint probability law has exactly the two prescribed marginals. expectedDistanceCosts consists of its finite expected distances, and wassersteinOneReal takes their infimum with an explicit nonempty finite-cost witness. The target is therefore the source earth-mover bound W1(D(first),D(second)) <= epsilon dist(first,second) for all feasible parameter pairs. A finite source bound corresponds to this finite-cost infimum; infinite-cost couplings cannot lower it. In the inner-product paper use, parameter distance equals the norm of the difference, and the explicit sensitivity premise permits precisely nonnegative epsilon, including 0. No attainment of the infimum, finite support, or off-domain distribution is required.

AppliedModelingLib.MeasurePerformativeMo.label: AppliedModelingLib.MeasurePerformativeModelOn.decoupledPerformativeRisk
AppliedModelingLib.MeasurePerformativeMo.reason: Compared definition_2_3_performative_stability_and_decoupled_risk at cited publication:219-228 with the expanded integral and every listed model, risk, optimality, stability, and theorem-use display. The deployed argument selects dataLaw, while the evaluated argument selects the loss parameter, giving DPR(theta,theta-prime)=E under D(theta) of loss(Z,theta-prime). The model ensures integrability for these two independently chosen feasible arguments. The displayed diagonal call gives PR; the stability calls keep the law argument fixed; and optimality compares diagonals. All these uses preserve the source argument order, candidate quantifier, and feasible parameter set.

AppliedModelingLib.MeasurePerformativeMo.label: AppliedModelingLib.MeasurePerformativeModelOn.performativeRisk
AppliedModelingLib.MeasurePerformativeMo.reason: Compared definition_2_1_performative_optimality_and_risk at cited publication:161-172 with the expanded definition and every listed decoupled-risk, model, optimality, and theorem-use display. The same feasible parameter is passed as both arguments of decoupledPerformativeRisk, so PR(theta) is exactly E under D(theta) of loss(Z,theta). In optimality comparisons, the induced law and evaluated parameter therefore change together, preserving the source objective. The model supplies the needed diagonal integrability; neither this definition nor the displayed use introduces a unique minimizer or evaluates a parameter outside Theta.

AppliedModelingLib.measureDecoupledPerfo.label: AppliedModelingLib.measureDecoupledPerformativeRisk
AppliedModelingLib.measureDecoupledPerfo.reason: Definition 2.3 defines DPR(θ, θ′) = E_{Z∼D(θ)} ℓ(Z; θ′). The expanded Lean declaration is exactly the corresponding integral of model.loss z evaluatedParameter under model.dataLaw distributionParameter, preserving the distribution/evaluation parameter order; the model integrability condition only makes the expectation real-valued and does not change the definition.
